newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian provinces go slow on tobacco lawsuits.
newsitem.headline: Canadian provinces go slow on tobacco lawsuits.

text.p: Canada's provincial leaders opted Friday for a wait-and-see approach on whether to sue the tobacco industry, as 40 states in the United States have done.
At a two-day meeting in this Atlantic seaside resort, the provincial leaders agreed in the meanwhile to monitor British Columbia's effort to take on the industy.

British Columbia became the first government outside the United States to propose taking legal action against the tobacco industry to recover the costs of health care for treating smoking related illnesses.

The leaders aparently backed away from a proposal by British Columbia and four Atlantic provinces for the premiers to consider a unified legal attack on the cigarette makers -- similar to the approach adopted in the United States.

"I not sure there's a lot served by having 10 court actions, or 11 court actions or five court actions. We have one," Ontario premier Mike Harris told reporters at the close of the leaders' annual meeting.
Alberta Premier Ralph Klien, a smoker, on Thursday said it would hypocritical for the provinces to file lawsuits to collect damages from an industry that they also depend on for tax revenues.
